title: Enforce binary-safe proof artifacts and repo-root scratch hygiene
goal:
# Enforce binary-safe proof artifacts and repo-root scratch hygiene

## Context
Case study: KainBain task 5a38ad45-74a6-4d00-b6fd-a1796e5f4f1f (pretty markdown tasks with code blocks, mermaid diagrams, and image references). A Deep Review stage failed the branch for two worktree-hygiene defects: docs proof file pretty-proof.png was byte-corrupted (magic bytes efbfbd instead of PNG magic 89504e47; the file tool reported data instead of PNG, contradicting the implementation report validity claim), and a stray dead scratch file rt.mjs with a broken import was committed at the repo root. See docs/tasks/5a38ad45-74a6-4d00-b6fd-a1796e5f4f1f/deep-review-failure-20261114-093429.md and the round-3 review it cites. The likely mechanism is agents writing or rewriting binary files through text-oriented edit tools, plus committing ad-hoc scratch files instead of keeping them untracked or outside the repo.

## Steps
1. Add documented guidance for proof artifacts: binary files (PNG screenshots, etc.) must be written through a binary-safe path only, never through text edit tools; verify with magic bytes (89504e47 for PNG) and the file command before claiming validity.
2. Add a cheap automated check (CI step or pre-commit check) that rejects: (a) committed files at the repo root matching scratch patterns (*.mjs scratch, rt.*, etc.) unless explicitly allowlisted, and (b) files under docs proof paths whose magic bytes do not match their extension.
3. Correct the stale validity claim in the implementation report only if it is still wrong on the current branch; otherwise leave history untouched.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A corrupted PNG (wrong magic bytes) committed as proof fails the new check with a message naming the file and expected vs actual magic.
- [ ] A scratch file dropped at the repo root fails the new check or is blocked from commit.
- [ ] Valid PNG proof plus no stray root files passes the check.

## Notes
This ticket targets structural process failure (binary handling and worktree hygiene), not a retry of the pretty-tasks feature itself, which is reported complete. Human reviewers should be able to trust proof-file validity claims without byte-level re-verification.

reports.content:
# Implementation plan — binary-safe proof artifacts and repo-root scratch hygiene

Task `b1c069e0-1875-4aa7-b51d-4c4399b2be31`. Case study: task `5a38ad45`
pretty-tasks Deep Review failure (`deep-review-failure-20261114-093429.md`,
`review-20261114-round3.md`): a committed `pretty-proof.png` with UTF-8
replacement bytes (`ef bf bd` where `0x89` belongs; `file` → `data`) that
contradicted the implementation report's validity claim, plus a tracked dead
scratch file `rt.mjs` at the repo root.

## Goal

Make proof-file corruption and stray root scratch files structurally hard to
ship: documented binary-safe handling rules agents will actually see, plus a
cheap automated gate that fails loudly with a fix-it message. Human reviewers
must be able to trust proof validity claims without byte-level re-verification.

## Success criteria

- A committed proof PNG with wrong magic bytes fails the new check; the
  message names the file and shows expected vs actual magic.
- A scratch file at the repo root fails the new check or is blocked from commit.
- Valid PNG proof plus no stray root files passes the check.
- Guidance exists where agents look, and the stale-claim question (step 3) is
  resolved with byte evidence, touching history only if still wrong.

## Survey answers (SURVEY.md — questions were unanswered, defaults chosen here)

The survey on `origin/kb/b1c069e0-1875-4aa7-b51d-4c4399b2be31` records four
questions with `"answers": {}`. This plan resolves each; the implementer treats
these as binding defaults unless a human overrides them.

- **q1 — where does the guidance live?** Both places (survey option 3), with
  one canonical source and pointers elsewhere to prevent drift: normative rule
  in agent guidance (`docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` commit-hygiene section,
  pointed to from `agents.md`) plus a short checklist at the proof workflow
  (alongside the screenshot/proof capture docs; see Phase 3).
- **q2 — how strict is the check?** Block plus explain how to fix (option 3):
  non-zero exit in an automated gate, message names the file, expected vs
  actual magic (or the matched scratch pattern), and the exact remedy command.
- **q3 — which stray root files are stopped?** All three survey categories:
  ad-hoc scripts (`rt.*`, root `*.mjs`/`*.cjs` not allowlisted), temp notes
  and logs at root, and loose images outside proof folders. Enforcement is
  allowlist-based: legitimate root files are enumerated, everything else
  matching a scratch pattern fails.
- **q4 — what about the old false validity claim?** Fix it now only if still
  wrong (option 1, matching ticket step 3). Current-branch evidence (gathered
  2026-11-14, see Phase 0) says the claim is already corrected by banners and
  the PNG is valid — so the expected outcome is verify-and-leave-untouched,
  recorded with evidence. No new sidecar correction note.

## Key decisions (with rejected alternatives)

1. **Enforce in the automated gate, not (only) a git hook.** The repo has no
   hook infrastructure (no `.husky`, `.githooks`, or `pre-commit` config), and
   the KainBain engine — not the agent — performs stage-output commits, so a
   locally installed hook is not a reliable enforcement point for agent
   behavior. The check must live where automated stages run: a new
   `scripts/check-*.mjs` following the existing check-script convention,
   wired into `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (fast overlap window or Harness
   Self-Tests branch) with an `npm run` script and `tests/*.test.mjs` pinning
   it. A documented optional local hook may be offered as a convenience, but
   it is not the enforcement mechanism. Rejected: pre-commit-only (no infra,
   wrong enforcement point) and review-stage-only (human re-verification is
   what this ticket eliminates).
2. **Scan the worktree + tracked set, not just the staged diff.** The failure
   mode is bytes corrupted before commit by text-oriented edit tools
   (`.gitattributes *.png binary` did not help — corruption happened
   pre-commit). The check reads actual file bytes from disk and compares
   against tracked/expected files, so it catches corruption regardless of
   staging state. Rejected: `--cached`-only diff scan (misses worktree
   corruption an agent is about to claim as valid).
3. **One checker, two rule families, shared exit path.** Magic-byte validation
   (proof paths) and root scratch detection share one script, one allowlist
   file, and one failure format, so there is a single gate branch to maintain.
   Rejected: two separate scripts (double wiring, double docs).
4. **Extension→magic table covers at least PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP** (the
   extensions `.gitattributes` already marks binary), with PNG (`89504e47`)
   pinned first. Unknown extensions are skipped, never failed — the check is a
   corruption detector, not a file-type police. Proof paths: everything under
   `docs/tasks/*/`, plus any `*-proof.*` / `screenshot*` naming the repo
   already uses.

## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change

Phases 0–2 create the seams (evidence baseline, reusable pure-function checker
module, test harness placement). Phases 3–5 are the actual change (rules,
wiring, docs, claim resolution), each small because the seams exist.

## Steps

### Phase 0 — Evidence baseline (research, first because everything conditions on it)

0.1. Re-confirm the step-3 precondition on the implementation branch (do not
assume this plan's evidence transfers): `xxd -l 8` and `file` on
`docs/tasks/5a38ad45-74a6-4d00-b6fd-a1796e5f4f1f/pretty-proof.png`,
`git ls-files | grep -E '^(rt\.mjs|scratch)'`, and read the correction banners
at the top of `implementation-report-20261114.md` (lines 1–65 on the planning
branch already correct the stale inner claim at old step 3).
0.2. Inventory legitimate repo-root files (`git ls-files` depth-1 plus
root dotfiles) to seed the scratch-check allowlist without false positives.
0.3. Read one check-script pair end to end for convention
(`scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `tests/check-one-function-per-file.test.mjs`,
and the Harness Self-Tests file list in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`): export pure
functions from the script, test via `node --test`, register the test file in
the gate list.
- Depends on: nothing. Validates: step-3 decision, allowlist seed, wiring points.

### Phase 1 — Checker module with pure, testable core (the big build)

1.1. Create `scripts/check-proof-and-hygiene.mjs` (name follows
`check-*.mjs` convention; exact filename is the implementer's choice):
- `magicForExtension(ext)` — table: `.png` → `89504e47`,
  `.jpg`/`.jpeg` → `ffd8ff`, `.gif` → `47494638`, `.webp` → `52494646`
  (RIFF; note the 8-byte `WEBP` marker handling).
- `checkFileMagic(absPath)` — reads first 8 bytes with `fs.readFileSync`,
  returns `{ ok, expected, actual }`; missing/unreadable files and unknown
  extensions return `ok: true` with a `skipped` reason (never fail closed
  on what the check does not understand).
- `isProofPath(relPath)` — matches `docs/tasks/**` image extensions and
  `*-proof.*` / `screenshot*` names.
- `isRootScratch(relPath, allowlist)` — matches root-level scratch
  patterns (`rt.*`, `*.mjs`/`*.cjs` repro scripts, `*.log`, `*.tmp`,
  `*.png`/`*.jpg` loose images, `t1.json`-style ad-hoc notes) unless the
  exact path is allowlisted.
- `formatFailure(...)` — one line per violation:
  `path: expected magic <expected>, found <actual> (<remedy>)` or
  `path: root scratch file matching <pattern> (<remedy>)`, where remedy is
  the concrete fix (e.g. `restore via git checkout <ref> -- <path> and
  re-verify with xxd/file`, `move to scratch/ (gitignored) or delete`).
1.2. CLI behavior: exit 0 with a one-line PASS summary when clean; exit 1
listing every violation otherwise. Support `--root <dir>` (default: repo
root) so tests run it against fixture trees.
- Depends on: phase 0. This is the seam every later phase uses.

### Phase 2 — Tests and gate wiring (makes the change safe to land)

2.1. Add `tests/check-proof-and-hygiene.test.mjs` in the existing
`node:test` + `assert/strict` style: valid-PNG passes, corrupt-PNG fixture
(first byte `ef bf bd`) fails with expected-vs-actual message, each scratch
pattern fails, allowlisted root files pass, unknown extensions skip.
Register the file in the Harness Self-Tests branch list in
`scripts/run-tests.mjs` (the list is explicitly exhaustive — an unregistered
file silently never runs).
2.2. Add an `npm run` script (e.g. `check:proof-hygiene`) and a fast
low-priority branch in `buildBranches` (or fold into Harness Self-Tests if a
separate branch is judged too heavy — decide in implementation, record why).
Keep it dependency-free (Node stdlib only) so the branch never needs
workspace provisioning.
- Depends on: phase 1.

### Phase 3 — Guidance docs (q1: both places, one canonical source)

3.1. Canonical rule in `docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` under commit
hygiene: binary files (PNG screenshots, etc.) are written only through a
binary-safe path — never through text edit tools; verify with
`xxd -l 8` (expect `8950 4e47…` for PNG) and `file` before claiming
validity; ad-hoc scratch stays in `scratch/` (gitignored) or `/tmp`, never
at the repo root.
3.2. Short checklist at the proof workflow: next to whatever documents the
screenshot/proof capture flow (`scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs` usage docs
/ `npm run capture:screenshot`), pointing back to the canonical rule.
3.3. One-line pointer from `agents.md` if that file indexes agent hygiene
rules (check first; do not duplicate prose).
- Depends on: phase 0 (needs the corruption mechanism wording from the
  round-3 review). Small because phase 1 fixes the exact commands to quote.

### Phase 4 — Resolve the stale validity claim (ticket step 3)

4.1. If phase 0 shows the report still asserting validity of corrupt bytes:
correct the claim in place with a dated correction banner (same style as the
existing banners), citing `xxd`/`file` evidence.
4.2. If phase 0 confirms the current state (valid PNG, correction banners
present, `rt.mjs` gone): change nothing; record the verification evidence in
the stage report. History stays untouched.
- Depends on: phase 0 only; may run parallel with phases 1–3.

### Phase 5 — Acceptance rehearsal and report

5.1. Run the three acceptance scenarios against the real script (in a
throwaway fixture tree or temp worktree, never by corrupting the real PNG):
corrupt PNG → exit 1 naming file + expected vs actual; root scratch file →
exit 1; valid PNG + clean root → exit 0.
5.2. Run the full affected gates: the new `npm run` script, the Harness
Self-Tests branch, and `npm run test:unit` per the repo's testing guidance.
5.3. Stage report records: survey-default mapping (q1–q4), step-3 evidence
and outcome, and the exact commands a reviewer can re-run.

## Validation plan

| Work unit | Check | Expected evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 baseline | `xxd -l 8`, `file`, `git ls-files`, report read | Magic `89504e47`, `file` → PNG, no `rt.mjs`, banners present (or a concrete diff list if the branch moved) |
| Phase 1 checker | `node --test tests/check-proof-and-hygiene.test.mjs` | All new tests green; corrupt fixture message shows `expected 89504e47, found efbfbd…` |
| Phase 2 wiring | New `npm run` script + Harness Self-Tests branch | Gate branch PASS on clean tree; FAIL (exit 1) with fixture violations |
| Phase 3 docs | `npm run docs:check` (link checker covers edited docs) | PASS; prose reviewed for non-duplication |
| Phase 4 claim | Byte evidence quoted in stage report | Either a dated correction banner or a leave-untouched justification with `xxd`/`file` output |
| Acceptance | Script run over the three scenarios | exit 1 / exit 1 / exit 0 as specified |

Highest-risk validation: the gate actually runs the new test file
(`run-tests.mjs` uses an explicit file list — forgetting registration is a
silent pass). Mitigation: after wiring, temporarily break one fixture
expectation, confirm the gate branch goes red, then restore.

## Risks and open questions

- **Risk:** allowlist too narrow → false failures on legitimate new root
  files. Mitigation: seed from the phase-0.2 inventory; failure message tells
  the author exactly how to allowlist; keep patterns scratch-shaped
  (`rt.*`, ad-hoc scripts) rather than extension-broad.
- **Risk:** agents corrupt binaries again before any gate runs. The gate
  catches it at the next automated stage, but same-stage claims could still be
  wrong. Mitigation: the guidance (phase 3) makes `xxd`+`file` verification
  part of the claim procedure itself; review stages re-run the check.
- **Non-goals:** retrying or changing the pretty-tasks feature; touching
  `pretty-proof.png` bytes (it is valid on the planning branch); git-hook
  installation machinery; history rewrites of the 5a38ad45 reports.
- **Open questions:** none requiring human input — survey q1–q4 are defaulted
  above with rationale, and all remaining unknowns are branch-state facts for
  phase 0 to establish. If a human disagrees with a survey default, that is a
  one-line plan edit, not new research.

## Documentation plan

- Normative guidance: `docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` (+ pointer from
  `agents.md` if it indexes such rules).
- Workflow checklist: alongside the `capture:screenshot` / proof-capture docs.
- Machine-readable contract: the checker's `--help`/header comment and the
  allowlist file document patterns and escape hatches.
- Audit trail: stage report with survey mapping, step-3 byte evidence, and
  re-runnable commands.

reports.content:
# Install-safety review: binary-safe proof artifacts and repo-root scratch hygiene

Scope of the change (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`): 16 files — new `scripts/check-proof-and-hygiene.mjs` plus `tests/check-proof-and-hygiene.test.mjs`, new `scripts/allowlists/repo-root-files.json` and `scripts/baselines/proof-hygiene-known-violations.json`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (new `Proof Hygiene` branch + test registration), `package.json` (`check:proof-hygiene` script), `scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs` (comment only), `docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` / `agents.md` (guidance), `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` (updated branch list). No dependency versions changed; no runtime tree changed.

## Would existing installs break on update?

No. Checked each install-breakage vector:

- **No new dependencies.** `package.json` only adds the `check:proof-hygiene` script entry; `dependencies`/`devDependencies`/`overrides` are identical to the base, and `package-lock.json` / `frontend/package.json` show no diff, so `npm ci` resolves the same tree. No `postinstall`/`preinstall`/`prepare` hooks exist or were added.
- **Runtime tree untouched.** The versioned installer (`scripts/lib/runner-install-root.sh`) copies only `runner/`, `api/`, `shared/`, `version.json`. `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` shows zero changes under `runner/`, `api/`, `shared/`, `frontend/`, `deploy/`, `Dockerfile`, `publish.sh`, `startRunner.sh`; `runner/version.json` still reports `runnerVersion 0.1.0` and `package.json` still `1.0.0`. An update therefore lays a byte-identical runtime and cannot break installed runners at boot. No deletions (`--diff-filter=D` empty).
- **stdlib-only, engine-compatible.** The checker imports only `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` and uses no `.at(` or other post-Node-20 APIs. Engines require `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`, so it runs on every supported install. Importing it does not execute the scan (guarded by `invokedDirectly`); `node --check` passes on all three touched scripts.
- **Passes on the unmodified tree.** `node scripts/check-proof-and-hygiene.mjs` exits 0 in ~0.1s with `✓ proof artifacts and repo-root hygiene OK (11 known pre-existing issue(s) recorded in the baseline)`, and `npm run check:proof-hygiene` exits 0 with the same line. All 28 tracked root files (`git ls-files` depth-1) evaluate `isRootScratch` false against the empty allowlist, so no legitimate root file false-fails; the 11 baselined corrupt PNGs were verified corrupt on HEAD (`xxd -l 8` → `efbf bd50…`) and are covered same-path/same-bytes. The only new execution on `deploy.sh --prod` (via `./run-tests.sh --no-canary`) therefore does not block updates on a clean tree; it fails only on deliberately bad fixtures.
- **Acceptance rehearsal holds.** In throwaway `--root` fixture trees: valid PNG (`89504e47`) + clean root → exit 0; corrupt PNG (`efbfbd…`) → exit 1 naming the path with `expected magic 89504e47, found efbfbd…` plus the remedy; root `rt.mjs` → exit 1 naming the file and the `rt.*` pattern plus the remedy. `node --test tests/check-proof-and-hygiene.test.mjs` passes 63/63 and `node --test tests/run-tests.test.mjs` passes 35/35, including the new `Proof Hygiene` wiring assertions.
- **No gate regressions.** `node --test tests/install-runner-wrapper.test.mjs` passes 8/8 both with and without `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT` set (the historical 3 failures in the two `automated-tests-failure-20261114-*` reports pre-date the 19:52 `sandboxEnv` fix and are not caused by this change). `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` passes (71 files), and `check-one-function-per-file` / `check-jsdoc-example` both report PASS on the new script.
- **No output-contract break.** The gate gains one branch (12→13 with canary, 11→12 with `--no-canary`); `run-tests.test.mjs` was updated to pin the new count and `deploy.sh` consumes exit codes, not line counts. `scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs` changes are comments only, so the binary-safe capture path is unchanged.

## Verdict

Safe to update: existing installs resolve the same dependency tree, receive a byte-identical runtime tree, and the single new gate execution passes on the current tree in subsecond time. Intentional failures (corrupt proof, stray root scratch) are the feature, not breakage.

1|# Implementation plan — binary-safe proof artifacts and repo-root scratch hygiene
2|
3|Task `b1c069e0-1875-4aa7-b51d-4c4399b2be31`. Case study: task `5a38ad45`
4|pretty-tasks Deep Review failure (`deep-review-failure-20261114-093429.md`,
5|`review-20261114-round3.md`): a committed `pretty-proof.png` with UTF-8
6|replacement bytes (`ef bf bd` where `0x89` belongs; `file` → `data`) that
7|contradicted the implementation report's validity claim, plus a tracked dead
8|scratch file `rt.mjs` at the repo root.
9|
10|## Goal
11|
12|Make proof-file corruption and stray root scratch files structurally hard to
13|ship: documented binary-safe handling rules agents will actually see, plus a
14|cheap automated gate that fails loudly with a fix-it message. Human reviewers
15|must be able to trust proof validity claims without byte-level re-verification.
16|
17|## Success criteria
18|
19|- A committed proof PNG with wrong magic bytes fails the new check; the
20|  message names the file and shows expected vs actual magic.
21|- A scratch file at the repo root fails the new check or is blocked from commit.
22|- Valid PNG proof plus no stray root files passes the check.
23|- Guidance exists where agents look, and the stale-claim question (step 3) is
24|  resolved with byte evidence, touching history only if still wrong.
25|
26|## Survey answers (SURVEY.md — questions were unanswered, defaults chosen here)
27|
28|The survey on `origin/kb/b1c069e0-1875-4aa7-b51d-4c4399b2be31` records four
29|questions with `"answers": {}`. This plan resolves each; the implementer treats
30|these as binding defaults unless a human overrides them.
31|
32|- **q1 — where does the guidance live?** Both places (survey option 3), with
33|  one canonical source and pointers elsewhere to prevent drift: normative rule
34|  in agent guidance (`docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` commit-hygiene section,
35|  pointed to from `agents.md`) plus a short checklist at the proof workflow
36|  (alongside the screenshot/proof capture docs; see Phase 3).
37|- **q2 — how strict is the check?** Block plus explain how to fix (option 3):
38|  non-zero exit in an automated gate, message names the file, expected vs
39|  actual magic (or the matched scratch pattern), and the exact remedy command.
40|- **q3 — which stray root files are stopped?** All three survey categories:
41|  ad-hoc scripts (`rt.*`, root `*.mjs`/`*.cjs` not allowlisted), temp notes
42|  and logs at root, and loose images outside proof folders. Enforcement is
43|  allowlist-based: legitimate root files are enumerated, everything else
44|  matching a scratch pattern fails.
45|- **q4 — what about the old false validity claim?** Fix it now only if still
46|  wrong (option 1, matching ticket step 3). Current-branch evidence (gathered
47|  2026-11-14, see Phase 0) says the claim is already corrected by banners and
48|  the PNG is valid — so the expected outcome is verify-and-leave-untouched,
49|  recorded with evidence. No new sidecar correction note.
50|
51|## Key decisions (with rejected alternatives)
52|
53|1. **Enforce in the automated gate, not (only) a git hook.** The repo has no
54|   hook infrastructure (no `.husky`, `.githooks`, or `pre-commit` config), and
55|   the KainBain engine — not the agent — performs stage-output commits, so a
56|   locally installed hook is not a reliable enforcement point for agent
57|   behavior. The check must live where automated stages run: a new
58|   `scripts/check-*.mjs` following the existing check-script convention,
59|   wired into `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (fast overlap window or Harness
60|   Self-Tests branch) with an `npm run` script and `tests/*.test.mjs` pinning
61|   it. A documented optional local hook may be offered as a convenience, but
62|   it is not the enforcement mechanism. Rejected: pre-commit-only (no infra,
63|   wrong enforcement point) and review-stage-only (human re-verification is
64|   what this ticket eliminates).
65|2. **Scan the worktree + tracked set, not just the staged diff.** The failure
66|   mode is bytes corrupted before commit by text-oriented edit tools
67|   (`.gitattributes *.png binary` did not help — corruption happened
68|   pre-commit). The check reads actual file bytes from disk and compares
69|   against tracked/expected files, so it catches corruption regardless of
70|   staging state. Rejected: `--cached`-only diff scan (misses worktree
71|   corruption an agent is about to claim as valid).
72|3. **One checker, two rule families, shared exit path.** Magic-byte validation
73|   (proof paths) and root scratch detection share one script, one allowlist
74|   file, and one failure format, so there is a single gate branch to maintain.
75|   Rejected: two separate scripts (double wiring, double docs).
76|4. **Extension→magic table covers at least PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP** (the
77|   extensions `.gitattributes` already marks binary), with PNG (`89504e47`)
78|   pinned first. Unknown extensions are skipped, never failed — the check is a
79|   corruption detector, not a file-type police. Proof paths: everything under
80|   `docs/tasks/*/`, plus any `*-proof.*` / `screenshot*` naming the repo
81|   already uses.
82|
83|## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
84|
85|Phases 0–2 create the seams (evidence baseline, reusable pure-function checker
86|module, test harness placement). Phases 3–5 are the actual change (rules,
87|wiring, docs, claim resolution), each small because the seams exist.
88|
89|## Steps
90|
91|### Phase 0 — Evidence baseline (research, first because everything conditions on it)
92|
93|0.1. Re-confirm the step-3 precondition on the implementation branch (do not
94|assume this plan's evidence transfers): `xxd -l 8` and `file` on
95|`docs/tasks/5a38ad45-74a6-4d00-b6fd-a1796e5f4f1f/pretty-proof.png`,
96|`git ls-files | grep -E '^(rt\.mjs|scratch)'`, and read the correction banners
97|at the top of `implementation-report-20261114.md` (lines 1–65 on the planning
98|branch already correct the stale inner claim at old step 3).
99|0.2. Inventory legitimate repo-root files (`git ls-files` depth-1 plus
100|root dotfiles) to seed the scratch-check allowlist without false positives.
101|0.3. Read one check-script pair end to end for convention
102|(`scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `tests/check-one-function-per-file.test.mjs`,
103|and the Harness Self-Tests file list in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`): export pure
104|functions from the script, test via `node --test`, register the test file in
105|the gate list.
106|- Depends on: nothing. Validates: step-3 decision, allowlist seed, wiring points.
107|
108|### Phase 1 — Checker module with pure, testable core (the big build)
109|
110|1.1. Create `scripts/check-proof-and-hygiene.mjs` (name follows
111|`check-*.mjs` convention; exact filename is the implementer's choice):
112|- `magicForExtension(ext)` — table: `.png` → `89504e47`,
113|  `.jpg`/`.jpeg` → `ffd8ff`, `.gif` → `47494638`, `.webp` → `52494646`
114|  (RIFF; note the 8-byte `WEBP` marker handling).
115|- `checkFileMagic(absPath)` — reads first 8 bytes with `fs.readFileSync`,
116|  returns `{ ok, expected, actual }`; missing/unreadable files and unknown
117|  extensions return `ok: true` with a `skipped` reason (never fail closed
118|  on what the check does not understand).
119|- `isProofPath(relPath)` — matches `docs/tasks/**` image extensions and
120|  `*-proof.*` / `screenshot*` names.
121|- `isRootScratch(relPath, allowlist)` — matches root-level scratch
122|  patterns (`rt.*`, `*.mjs`/`*.cjs` repro scripts, `*.log`, `*.tmp`,
123|  `*.png`/`*.jpg` loose images, `t1.json`-style ad-hoc notes) unless the
124|  exact path is allowlisted.
125|- `formatFailure(...)` — one line per violation:
126|  `path: expected magic <expected>, found <actual> (<remedy>)` or
127|  `path: root scratch file matching <pattern> (<remedy>)`, where remedy is
128|  the concrete fix (e.g. `restore via git checkout <ref> -- <path> and
129|  re-verify with xxd/file`, `move to scratch/ (gitignored) or delete`).
130|1.2. CLI behavior: exit 0 with a one-line PASS summary when clean; exit 1
131|listing every violation otherwise. Support `--root <dir>` (default: repo
132|root) so tests run it against fixture trees.
133|- Depends on: phase 0. This is the seam every later phase uses.
134|
135|### Phase 2 — Tests and gate wiring (makes the change safe to land)
136|
137|2.1. Add `tests/check-proof-and-hygiene.test.mjs` in the existing
138|`node:test` + `assert/strict` style: valid-PNG passes, corrupt-PNG fixture
139|(first byte `ef bf bd`) fails with expected-vs-actual message, each scratch
140|pattern fails, allowlisted root files pass, unknown extensions skip.
141|Register the file in the Harness Self-Tests branch list in
142|`scripts/run-tests.mjs` (the list is explicitly exhaustive — an unregistered
143|file silently never runs).
144|2.2. Add an `npm run` script (e.g. `check:proof-hygiene`) and a fast
145|low-priority branch in `buildBranches` (or fold into Harness Self-Tests if a
146|separate branch is judged too heavy — decide in implementation, record why).
147|Keep it dependency-free (Node stdlib only) so the branch never needs
148|workspace provisioning.
149|- Depends on: phase 1.
150|
151|### Phase 3 — Guidance docs (q1: both places, one canonical source)
152|
153|3.1. Canonical rule in `docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` under commit
154|hygiene: binary files (PNG screenshots, etc.) are written only through a
155|binary-safe path — never through text edit tools; verify with
156|`xxd -l 8` (expect `8950 4e47…` for PNG) and `file` before claiming
157|validity; ad-hoc scratch stays in `scratch/` (gitignored) or `/tmp`, never
158|at the repo root.
159|3.2. Short checklist at the proof workflow: next to whatever documents the
160|screenshot/proof capture flow (`scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs` usage docs
161|/ `npm run capture:screenshot`), pointing back to the canonical rule.
162|3.3. One-line pointer from `agents.md` if that file indexes agent hygiene
163|rules (check first; do not duplicate prose).
164|- Depends on: phase 0 (needs the corruption mechanism wording from the
165|  round-3 review). Small because phase 1 fixes the exact commands to quote.
166|
167|### Phase 4 — Resolve the stale validity claim (ticket step 3)
168|
169|4.1. If phase 0 shows the report still asserting validity of corrupt bytes:
170|correct the claim in place with a dated correction banner (same style as the
171|existing banners), citing `xxd`/`file` evidence.
172|4.2. If phase 0 confirms the current state (valid PNG, correction banners
173|present, `rt.mjs` gone): change nothing; record the verification evidence in
174|the stage report. History stays untouched.
175|- Depends on: phase 0 only; may run parallel with phases 1–3.
176|
177|### Phase 5 — Acceptance rehearsal and report
178|
179|5.1. Run the three acceptance scenarios against the real script (in a
180|throwaway fixture tree or temp worktree, never by corrupting the real PNG):
181|corrupt PNG → exit 1 naming file + expected vs actual; root scratch file →
182|exit 1; valid PNG + clean root → exit 0.
183|5.2. Run the full affected gates: the new `npm run` script, the Harness
184|Self-Tests branch, and `npm run test:unit` per the repo's testing guidance.
185|5.3. Stage report records: survey-default mapping (q1–q4), step-3 evidence
186|and outcome, and the exact commands a reviewer can re-run.
187|
188|## Validation plan
189|
190|| Work unit | Check | Expected evidence |
191||---|---|---|
192|| Phase 0 baseline | `xxd -l 8`, `file`, `git ls-files`, report read | Magic `89504e47`, `file` → PNG, no `rt.mjs`, banners present (or a concrete diff list if the branch moved) |
193|| Phase 1 checker | `node --test tests/check-proof-and-hygiene.test.mjs` | All new tests green; corrupt fixture message shows `expected 89504e47, found efbfbd…` |
194|| Phase 2 wiring | New `npm run` script + Harness Self-Tests branch | Gate branch PASS on clean tree; FAIL (exit 1) with fixture violations |
195|| Phase 3 docs | `npm run docs:check` (link checker covers edited docs) | PASS; prose reviewed for non-duplication |
196|| Phase 4 claim | Byte evidence quoted in stage report | Either a dated correction banner or a leave-untouched justification with `xxd`/`file` output |
197|| Acceptance | Script run over the three scenarios | exit 1 / exit 1 / exit 0 as specified |
198|
199|Highest-risk validation: the gate actually runs the new test file
200|(`run-tests.mjs` uses an explicit file list — forgetting registration is a
201|silent pass). Mitigation: after wiring, temporarily break one fixture
202|expectation, confirm the gate branch goes red, then restore.
203|
204|## Risks and open questions
205|
206|- **Risk:** allowlist too narrow → false failures on legitimate new root
207|  files. Mitigation: seed from the phase-0.2 inventory; failure message tells
208|  the author exactly how to allowlist; keep patterns scratch-shaped
209|  (`rt.*`, ad-hoc scripts) rather than extension-broad.
210|- **Risk:** agents corrupt binaries again before any gate runs. The gate
211|  catches it at the next automated stage, but same-stage claims could still be
212|  wrong. Mitigation: the guidance (phase 3) makes `xxd`+`file` verification
213|  part of the claim procedure itself; review stages re-run the check.
214|- **Non-goals:** retrying or changing the pretty-tasks feature; touching
215|  `pretty-proof.png` bytes (it is valid on the planning branch); git-hook
216|  installation machinery; history rewrites of the 5a38ad45 reports.
217|- **Open questions:** none requiring human input — survey q1–q4 are defaulted
218|  above with rationale, and all remaining unknowns are branch-state facts for
219|  phase 0 to establish. If a human disagrees with a survey default, that is a
220|  one-line plan edit, not new research.
221|
222|## Documentation plan
223|
224|- Normative guidance: `docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` (+ pointer from
225|  `agents.md` if it indexes such rules).
226|- Workflow checklist: alongside the `capture:screenshot` / proof-capture docs.
227|- Machine-readable contract: the checker's `--help`/header comment and the
228|  allowlist file document patterns and escape hatches.
229|- Audit trail: stage report with survey mapping, step-3 byte evidence, and
230|  re-runnable commands.
